title: Giants of the Outer Dark
objective: After this level you can tell gas giants from ice giants and describe Jupiter's and Saturn's standout features.
summary: Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants, Uranus and Neptune are ice giants. Jupiter outweighs every other planet combined, and Saturn's rings are mostly ice.

cards.headline: Past Mars, the planets stop being rocky and start being enormous.

items.label: Gas giants
points: No solid surface to stand on

items.label: Ice giants
points: Rich in water, ammonia and methane 'ices'

cards.fact: Jupiter has more than twice the mass of all the other planets combined.
cards.context: If the planets were a team, Jupiter would be carrying it.

cards.headline: Saturn's rings are ice
cards.body: Those famous rings aren't solid. They're countless chunks of water ice, with some rock, ranging from dust-sized grains to pieces as big as houses. Each chunk orbits Saturn on its own path, like a tiny moon.

cards.headline: Outer solar system: mapped
learned: Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants
Uranus and Neptune are ice giants
Jupiter outweighs all other planets combined

questions.prompt: Which pair are the ice giants?
questions.explanation: Uranus and Neptune are the ice giants; Jupiter and Saturn are the gas giants.

questions.prompt: Why couldn't you land on Jupiter or Saturn?

options.label: Their surfaces are covered in deep, sticky mud
options.rationale: There’s no surface at all: the gas just gets denser.

options.label: They have no solid surface, just ever-thicker gas
Their rings form a solid barrier around them
options.rationale: Rings are loose chunks of ice and rock, not a wall.

options.label: Their gravity is too weak to land safely
options.rationale: Their gravity is strong; the problem is there’s nothing solid.

questions.explanation: Gas giants are mostly hydrogen and helium. Descend and the gas just gets denser and hotter, with no ground to stand on.

questions.prompt: From Level 3: what's the big difference between the inner planets and the outer giants?

options.label: Inner planets are big and gassy; giants are small and icy
The giants all orbit closer to the Sun than the inner planets
options.rationale: The giants orbit much farther out.

options.label: Inner planets are small and rocky; giants are mostly gas and ice
Only the inner planets have moons; the giants have none

questions.explanation: The solar system splits neatly: four small rocky worlds inside, four giants of gas and ice outside.
